newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN chief expects movement on Iraq deal in weeks.
newsitem.headline: UN chief expects movement on Iraq deal in weeks.

text.p: Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali expects some movement on the Iraqi's oil for food deal in the next few weeks but says there is still work to be done, U.N. spokeswoman Sylvana Foa told reporters on Monday.
"There is still work to be done but he is optimistic there will be movement in the next few weeks," she quoted him as saying.
Foa confirmed Iraq had sent a letter to the United Nations, that, in effect, said it "agrees with the views of the U.N. secretariat" on how the deal should be implemented.
Foa said "there are still steps" to be taken. She said the details all needed to be in place before Boutros-Ghali would give the go-ahead on the deal.

Iraqi U.N. Ambassador Nizar Hamdoon said earlier that Baghdad had agreed to all U.N. conditions that had held up implementation of the oil-for-food deal and predicted oil could start flowing in December.

He was speaking to reporters after a meeting with Undersecretary-General Chinmaya Gharekhan, who heads a U.N. task force overseeing the deal, which would permit the sale of $2 billion of Iraqi oil over six months on a renewable basis.
